name: find_sessions
description: The coding sessions you can message on your team's lightbulb network (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok CLI, OpenCode): this computer's, then your teammates'. status is busy, waiting (waiting_for says for what; its person must answer), idle, or ended. Ended sessions stay seven days with ended_at and reason; this computer's carry resume, the command that resumes them. An ended session reads nothing unless resumed; a message to one waits a day. online false with seen_at is a computer that is offline (messages wait). Pass one's session_id as send_message session_id; is_this_session marks your own: never message it.

query.description: Text to find (case-insensitive) in a session's id, agent, folder, repo, branch, title, task, person or computer. Empty lists all.

name: send_message
description: Sends text to session_id (a coding session from find_sessions, on this computer or a teammate's, sent peer to peer). reply_to (the request_id of a message you got from check_inbox) answers that message; reply_to alone replies to whoever sent it. request_id: a new [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128} string; reuse it only to retry that same send. Returns its receipt; its note says where the message waits. Answering an assignment (reply_to its request_id) makes your reply its result; add status if it is not done.

request_id.description: A new [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128} string; reuse it only to retry this send.

reply_to.description: The request_id of the message this answers.

status.description: Only when answering an assignment: how it ended. Absent means done.

name: message_receipt
description: The receipt of a message you sent, by its request_id, including when the send's answer was lost.

request_id.description: The request_id of a message you sent.

name: check_inbox
description: Takes the messages sent to you on the team's lightbulb network, first waiting up to wait_secs for one; one call may return sooner, so call again to keep waiting. Each message has its raw text and, in framed, the text as delivered; pass its request id as send_message reply_to to answer it.

wait_secs.description: Wait up to this many seconds for a message to arrive.

name: find_workers
description: The agents that take an assignment: teammates' computers that start fresh workers once they opt in. Pass one's session_id to assign.

query.description: Text to find (case-insensitive) in a worker's id, agent, folder, repo, branch, title, task, person or computer. Empty lists all.

name: assign
description: Hands a job to one agent: to is a session_id from find_sessions or find_workers. brief says what to do, done_when says what finished looks like, deadline_s (default 3600, at most 14400) bounds it. The reply is the result: it arrives in check_inbox as kind "result" with a status, and message_receipt shows it under result. request_id: a new [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128} string.

request_id.description: A new [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128} string; reuse it only to retry this assignment.

to.description: A session_id from find_sessions or find_workers.

repo.description: The repository the job is in, if any.

branch.description: The branch to work on, if any.

name: cancel_assignment
description: Cancels an assignment you sent, by its request_id. The agent is told to stop and reply with status "cancelled". request_id: a new id for this cancel.

assignment.description: The request_id of the assignment you sent.

request_id.description: A new id for this cancel; reuse it only to retry.

name: recall
description: Call when a task starts or you need something a teammate may know, not on every turn: the answer is one page of about 8,000 tokens, up to about 9,000 on a full page. It also includes excerpts from your own prompts and replies in this repository on this computer, or in every repository when the folder has no git origin.

name: remember
description: Returns what is already known on the subject; call again with `replaces` if yours is a change. Personal unless the person says to share
